comment: Indicators that fall on one of the 10,000 most visited domains (Tranco list) are reviewed by hand before a release: a spyware domain is almost never that popular, so a match usually means a shared service or a mainstream app. The compiler refuses to sign while a popular indicator has no decision here. 'keep' signs it as published, 'monitoring' signs it as a monitoring app people often install knowingly (a point to review, never a detection), 'drop' leaves it out; 'except' lists hosts of a kept domain that are dropped.

life360.com.reason: Life360's own servers, published as a monitoring app (watchware): already a point to review.

tile-api.com.reason: Life360 development hosts, published as a monitoring app (watchware).

qustodio.com.reason: Qustodio's own site, published as a monitoring app (watchware).

mobile-tracker-free.com.reason: The stalkerware vendor's own site and servers; popular because it is sold widely.

findmykids.org.reason: A parental-control app sold in the app stores; the source lists it both as stalkerware and as a monitoring app.

umeng.com.reason: An analytics SDK used by thousands of ordinary apps, not Cocospy's own server.

wondershare.com.reason: FamiSafe's own hosts are kept; the account and analytics hosts serve every Wondershare product.

wondershare.cc.reason: Wondershare's shared app backend, used by all its products.
